{{Short description|Geometry concept}}
{{distinguish|Alexandrov topology}}

In [[differential geometry]], '''Alexandrov spaces with curvature ≥ ''k''''' form a generalization of [[Riemannian manifold]]s with [[Curvature of Riemannian manifolds|sectional curvature]] ≥ ''k'', where ''k'' is some real number. By definition, these spaces are [[Locally compact space|locally compact]] [[Complete metric space|complete]] [[length space]]s where the lower curvature bound is defined via comparison of [[geodesic triangle]]s in the space to geodesic triangles in standard constant-curvature Riemannian surfaces.<ref name=shio>{{cite conference|url=http://www.math.psu.edu/petrunin/papers/akp-papers/shiohama_1.pdf|title=An Introduction to the Geometry of Alexandrov Spaces|author=Kathusiro Shiohama|conference=Daewoo Workshop on Differential Geometry|location=Kwang Won University, Chunchon, Korea|date=  July 13–17, 1992}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Aleksandrov|first=A D|last2=Berestovskii|first2=V N|last3=Nikolaev|first3=I G|date=1986-01-01|title=Generalized Riemannian spaces|journal=Russian Mathematical Surveys|language=en|volume=41|issue=3|pages=1–54|doi=10.1070/rm1986v041n03abeh003311|issn=0036-0279}}</ref>

One can show that the [[Hausdorff dimension]] of an Alexandrov space with curvature ≥ ''k'' is either a non-negative integer or infinite.<ref name=shio/> One can define a notion of "angle" (see [[Comparison triangle#Alexandrov angles]]) and "tangent cone" in these spaces.

Alexandrov spaces with curvature ≥ ''k'' are important as they form the limits (in the [[Gromov–Hausdorff metric]]) of sequences of Riemannian manifolds with sectional curvature ≥ ''k'',<ref name=berger/> as described by [[Gromov's compactness theorem (geometry)|Gromov's compactness theorem]].

Alexandrov spaces with curvature ≥ ''k'' were introduced by the Russian mathematician [[Aleksandr Danilovich Aleksandrov]] in 1948<ref name=berger>{{cite book |last=Berger |first=Marcel |date=2003 |title=A Panoramic View of Riemannian Geometry |publisher= Springer|page=704}}</ref> and should not be confused with [[Alexandrov topology|Alexandrov-discrete spaces]] named after the Russian topologist [[P. S. Alexandrov|Pavel Alexandrov]]. They were studied in detail by [[Yuri Burago|Burago]], [[Mikhail Leonidovich Gromov|Gromov]] and [[Grigori Perelman|Perelman]] in 1992<ref name=burago>{{cite journal |last1=Burago |first1=Yuri |last2=Gromov |first2= Mikhail Leonidovich|last3=Perelman |first3=Grigori|date= 1992|title=A.D. Alexandrov spaces with curvature bounded below |journal=  Russian Math. Surveys|volume=47 |issue=2 |pages= 1–58|doi=10.1070/RM1992v047n02ABEH000877 }}</ref> and were later used in Perelman's proof of the [[Poincaré conjecture]].
